leads.title: First DuckDB release containing the #12596 fix
leads.detail: Fix merged to main 2024-06-24 [S10]; v1.0.0 tag commit 2024-05-29 predates it, v1.1.0 tag commit 2024-09-08 postdates it [S12, S13]. Whether any 1.0.x bugfix release (e.g. 1.0.1/1.0.2) carried the fix was not established.
leads.next_step: diff tags v1.0.x against merge commit 2532c30f or read release notes for the 1.0.x series

leads.title: null_padding default value discrepancy
leads.detail: PR #6765 body says null_padding 'defaults to true, which mimicks the behavior of Pandas/Polars' [S1]; the current docs' sample error block prints 'null_padding=0' [S2]. Probably a flag-style rendering (0/1) vs prose, but per-version default behavior was not verified.
leads.next_step: run read_csv against a short-row CSV on pinned DuckDB versions 0.8/1.0/1.4+ and observe

leads.title: devguide branches.csv / end-of-life.csv source location
leads.detail: versions.rst references include/branches.csv via csv-table :file:, but include/ on main contains only activate-tab.rst and links.rst; raw fetches 404 [S22]. Exact EOL dates were taken from endoflife.date [S16] instead.
leads.next_step: locate the csv-table includes (build-time substitution?) or pin the rendered page's table HTML

leads.title: Jupyter kernel-restart output-clearing behavior and settings
leads.detail: Whether Jupyter Notebook/Lab clears or preserves outputs on kernel restart (and under which settings) was not researched; it affects UI defaults for the 'restart marks unverified' rule.
leads.next_step: inspect jupyterlab/notebook restart handlers and settings schema

leads.title: DuckDB out-of-core behavior for global operators on the 8-core/16 GB envelope
leads.detail: Buffer-pool eviction under a memory limit is evidenced in tagged source [S13] and bounded CSV reading in docs [S2], but 5 GB sort/distinct behavior (spill vs failure, disk usage) was never measured.

leads.title: marimo #9881 (replayed cached outputs without live-vs-cached provenance)
leads.detail: Open bug (2026-06-14) assigned to a maintainer; directly parallels this proposal's provenance-badge requirement. Fix approach unknown.
leads.next_step: watch for the fix; adopt any generation/provenance mechanism they land on

leads.title: marimo PR #10915 (cross-app state staleness, closes #10602)
leads.detail: PR closed 2026-10-05 with merged_at null; whether it was reworked/abandoned is unknown. Evidence value: demonstrates cross-context staleness dispatch is genuinely hard.
leads.next_step: recheck issue #10602 state before relying on either approach

leads.title: Multi-writer collaboration via Quack protocol or DuckLake
leads.detail: Quack remote protocol beta as of DuckDB v1.5.2; DuckLake (Postgres catalog) presented as the stable multi-writer route [S3]. Out of scope for a local-first small team.
leads.next_step: revisit only if real-time collaboration becomes a requirement

leads.title: ipyflow as a reactive layer over existing Jupyter kernels
leads.detail: Cited by marimo's README as part of the reactive-dataflow lineage [S5]; would be the natural alternative if staleness must be added to unmodified Jupyter kernels rather than a separate status layer.
leads.next_step: compare ipyflow's dataflow tracking granularity vs static refs/defs

leads.title: nbformat/Jupyter trust model and signed notebooks
leads.detail: The Jupyter 'trusted notebook' mechanism interacts with 'browsing must not execute'; whether to adopt, ignore, or warn on trust flags was left open.
leads.next_step: read nbformat trust/signature docs and Jupyter security docs

leads.title: Sandbox mechanism selection for the production execution boundary
leads.detail: This research's sandbox (bubblewrap/systemd namespaces, per-receipt limits) proves the pattern is workable but the production mechanism (bubblewrap vs nsjail vs containers) was not chosen or benchmarked; Windows story unresolved.
leads.next_step: validation V7 (escape-attempt suite) per candidate mechanism; define Windows fallback (job objects + restricted tokens) or document Linux/macOS-first scope
